title: Half-month Sprint — Lean OKR Experiment Log
content:
Half-month Sprint: 2026-02-01 — 2026-02-14
Owner: Miru Kato
Purpose: run a lean OKR + habit experiment to trade a small amount of throughput for cleaner signals and lower cognitive overhead. This is a personal operationalization: what I _actually_ do for the next two weeks and how I measure it.

Context and motivation
- Burnout drift: last quarter I stretched across three parallel projects and lost momentum on measurable outputs.
- Hypothesis: swapping one broad throughput goal for two tight leading indicators (daily focused blocks + async prioritization) will improve week-over-week visible output without increasing hours.
- Constraints: still on-call rotationally, two recurring cross-team meetings (Mon/Wed), limited focus windows before midday.

Compact OKR (lean)
- Objective: Ship higher-quality, predictable output from my micro-projects each sprint.
  - Key result 1 (KR1 - leading): 8/10 weekdays with a 90+ minute uninterrupted focus block focused on project A (focus blocks tracked via calendar tags).
  - Key result 2 (KR2 - leading): Reduce context-switching by 40% measured as fewer >2 distinct task switches in an afternoon (tracked via manual end-of-day log).
  - Key result 3 (KR3 - lagging): Deliver 2 merged PRs related to performance tuning or observability for project A by end of sprint.

Hypotheses (explicit)
- H1: If I enforce a single 90+ minute morning block and a 30-minute afternoon review, then I will finish the day with clearer next steps and fewer unfinished tickets. (measure: EOD checklist + number of tickets left in progress)
- H2: If I reduce meetings in the first three hours to <30 minutes total, then the first focus block completion rate increases from ~40% to ~80%.
- H3: If I batch small review tasks to two specific 30-minute slots, then context-switching metric will fall by ~40% and perceived mental fatigue will drop (self-report 1-5).

Measurement approach (practical)
- Daily micro-log template (EOD):
  - Focus block achieved? (yes/no)
  - Primary deliverable advanced (short description)
  - Tickets left in progress (count)
  - Energy (1-5)
  - Blockers/interruptions (short)
- Weekly roll-up: count days with focus block, avg tickets left, #context switches (manual), merged PRs, qualitative notes.

Experiment wiring (tools + calendar)
- Calendar: block 9:00–10:40 as "FOCUS: Project A (no meetings)" with 'busy' visibility and a short owner note.
- Slack: set status "heads down" and enable do-not-disturb during the focus block.
- GitHub: label small PRs as "mini-deliverable" to batch reviews.
- Simple spreadsheet row per day (manual) — I prefer quick manual logging to force reflection.

Daily sprint log (high level samples)
- 2026-02-01: Focus block achieved. Pulled metrics baseline for caching layer. 1 ticket left. Energy 4. Blockers: none.
- 2026-02-02: Missed morning block due to 1:1 scheduling misalignment (rescheduled). Did afternoon review. 3 tickets left. Energy 2.
- 2026-02-05: Focus block achieved; implemented local perf test harness; exploratory PR opened (mini-deliverable). Energy 4.
- 2026-02-09: Partial block (60m) because of paging; documented fallbacks for the test harness. Energy 3.
- 2026-02-12: Full block; merged infra improvements PR (1 of 2). Energy 5.

What worked (patterns observed)
- Blocking the calendar was the single most effective lever — when respected by others it eliminated early fragmentation.
- Manual EOD reflection forced immediate triage of unfinished work; I shipped clearer next-action items.
- Batching review tasks into two slots reduced review thrash; reviewers reacted positively when PRs were labeled.

What didn't work / risks
- On-call pages break the morning block — need a micro-strategy for keeping a short recovery routine to return to deep work.
- Meetings still bleed into focus windows when invited last-minute. Need to pushback and propose alternatives (async notes).
- Manual context-switch counting is noisy — will need a simpler proxy next sprint (e.g., number of distinct Jira tickets touched after 1pm).

Decisions and changes mid-sprint
- Added a "30-minute recovery ritual" after any page to rebuild context: 5m notes, 10m quick re-open of code, 15m focused work.
- Committed to explicitly decline meetings that land in the 9:00–10:40 block and offer two concrete async options instead.

Concrete outcomes (end of this half-month)
- KR1: Focus block achieved 9 out of 10 scheduled weekdays (90%) — strong signal.
- KR2: Manual context-switch metric dropped ~35% (near target but noisy).
- KR3: 1 merged PR (infra/perf) and 1 open mini-PR (in review) — one short of target but meaningful progress.

Confidence and trade-offs
- Confidence in causal link (calendar block -> output) is medium-high (4/5) based on pattern repetition.
- Trade-off: some async collaboration slowed (e.g., reviews took longer when batched) but overall output clarity improved.

Next sprint (two-week plan)
- Objective: Push KR3 to completion (merge second PR) and stabilize a lighter context-switch proxy.
- Tactics:
  - Keep morning block with stronger meeting pushback.
  - Introduce a single "Review hour" at 15:30 daily for 30 minutes to keep PR latency reasonable.
  - Replace manual context-switch counting with a simple metric: "distinct Jira issues with work logs >0 after 13:00" (weekly export).
  - Share a short note in #eng-productivity summarizing the experiment and invite feedback.

Personal commitments (contract)
- I will not schedule meetings into the 9:00–10:40 block for the next sprint unless urgent and accepted by me.
- I will do the EOD micro-log every weekday before leaving the workspace.
- I will run a quick synthesis on Friday and send a 5-line summary to Leah for accountability.

Quick wins for next week
- Add "mini-deliverable" label template to GitHub PR creation.
- Draft a short slack post (2–3 bullets) describing the experiment and ask for review timing preferences.
- Create a saved Jira filter for "issues touched after 13:00" to produce the context-switch proxy automatically.

Notes to self (unpolished)
- Keep the habit small: shipping one clean PR is better than partial progress across three.
- If on-call frequency increases, re-evaluate the morning block timing (maybe shift later).
- Bring the experiment language into 1:1s to get manager buy-in — explicit permission helps with meeting declines.

Questions to revisit at next retro
- Did batching reviews increase overall cycle time in a way that harms downstream teams? (collect PR review latency stats)
- Is the "distinct Jira issues after 13:00" metric a faithful proxy for context-switching?
- Can I automate any of the EOD fields (calendar integration, slack DND detection)?

Appendix
- Short daily template (copy into daily note): Focus block achieved? / Primary deliverable / tickets left / energy / blockers.
- Links: slack:#eng-productivity/batching-experiment, github:redwood/serve#9821, confluence:okrs/personal-templates

-- end of half-month log --

(Notes: rough, intentionally informal. This is my personal experiment log — will iterate and snapshot into Confluence if outcomes are repeatable.)
